# Coupled pilot

Run the pilot using `scripts/run_coupled_pilot.py`.

## Case Selection

You can select specific test cases from the suite using one or more `--case` flags.

### Examples
- Run all cases (no-filter default):
  ```bash
  python3 scripts/run_coupled_pilot.py --binary ... --repo ... --out ...
  ```
- Run specific cases using `--case`:
  ```bash
  python3 scripts/run_coupled_pilot.py --binary ... --repo ... --out ... --case alpha --case gamma
  ```

### Behavior and Rules
- **Original Suite Order**: Regardless of the order in which `--case` flags are passed on the command line (e.g., `--case gamma --case alpha`), selected cases are executed and recorded in their original suite order (`alpha` then `gamma`).
- **Duplicates**: Duplicate `--case` flags (e.g., `--case gamma --case alpha --case gamma`) are deduplicated so each named case runs exactly once.
- **Unknown IDs**: Any unknown case ID provided via `--case` is validated and fails immediately (exiting with an error) *before* any output directory is created or any test case is executed.
- **No-Filter Default**: When no `--case` flags are supplied, all cases in the suite are run.
- **No-Overwrite & Oracles**: The no-overwrite receipt guard and independent oracles are fully preserved.

## Selecting cases with --case

By default (no --case flags) the pilot runs every case in the suite.

Pass --case one or more times to run only the named cases:

    python3 scripts/run_coupled_pilot.py --case alpha --case gamma

This runs `alpha` and `gamma` only; `beta` is skipped.

Behavior of repeated --case flags:

- Each named case runs exactly once, even if you repeat the flag
  (e.g. `--case gamma --case alpha --case gamma` runs `alpha` and `gamma`,
  each a single time — duplicates are collapsed).
- Selected cases run in the original suite order, not the order you typed
  them. `--case gamma --case alpha` still runs `alpha` before `gamma`.
- An unknown case ID is an error: the pilot prints `Unknown case ID(s): ...`
  and exits non-zero before creating any output directory or executing any
  case.
- With no --case flags at all, every case in the suite runs (no filtering).

The existing no-overwrite guard still applies: if the output directory
